mcqs.question: The Telangana High Court disqualified Khairatabad MLA Danam Nagender with effect from which date under which provision?
options: April 23, 2024, under Paragraph 2(1)(a) of the Tenth Schedule
September 18, 2026, under Paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule
mcqs.explanation: Danam Nagender was disqualified with effect from April 23, 2024 under Paragraph 2(1)(a) of the Tenth Schedule. September 18, 2026 was the date of the High Court judgment, not the effective date of disqualification.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Under Paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule, the Speaker decides disqualification cases, subject to judicial review.
Statement B: Under Article 192, the Governor decides disqualification cases arising under the Tenth Schedule.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is correct: Paragraph 6 assigns the decision to the Speaker, subject to judicial review. Statement B is incorrect because Article 192 concerns other disqualifications, while High Courts review Tenth Schedule decisions under Article 226.

mcqs.question: Under the constitutional framework applicable to State ministries, what limit was introduced by the 91st Amendment, 2003?
options: Ministers may not exceed 15% of the Assembly strength, with a minimum of 12
Ministers may not exceed 10% of the Assembly strength, with a minimum of 15
Ministers may not exceed 15% of the Assembly strength, with a minimum of 10
Ministers may not exceed 20% of the Assembly strength, with a minimum of 12
mcqs.explanation: The 91st Amendment, 2003 limits a State ministry to 15% of the Assembly strength and prescribes a minimum of 12 ministers. The other options alter either the percentage or the minimum.

mcqs.question: In the action plan for a drug-free India, what approach was emphasised regarding drug trafficking?
options: Targeting whole networks and supply chains, along with strengthening the four-tier NCORD
Targeting only small offenders through a two-tier NCORD
Targeting only State-level offenders through a three-tier NCORD
Targeting only international suppliers through a single-tier NCORD
mcqs.explanation: The strategy emphasised targeting whole networks and supply chains rather than only small offenders, while strengthening the four-tier NCORD. The other options incorrectly narrow the target or change the NCORD structure.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II in relation to drug-control institutions, constitutional provisions and observances.

List-I
 a. Narcotics Control Bureau
 b. Article 47
 c. Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
 d. International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking

List-II
 i. 2020; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
 ii. June 26
 iii. 1986; Ministry of Home Affairs
 iv. Directive Principle concerning intoxicating substances
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-iv, c-i and d-ii. The NCB dates to 1986 under the Ministry of Home Affairs; Article 47 is the relevant Directive Principle; the Abhiyaan began in 2020; and the international observance is on June 26.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is an incorrect statement regarding the seven pillars of PRAHAAR?
options: Prevention is one of the pillars
Human Rights is one of the pillars
Recovery and Resilience is one of the pillars
Border Management is one of the pillars
mcqs.explanation: Border Management is not listed among PRAHAAR's seven pillars. The listed pillars include Prevention, Human Rights, and Recovery and Resilience.

mcqs.question:
Match the telecom approval arrangements with the corresponding authority or range.

List-I
 a. Projects examined earlier by the Digital Communications Commission
 b. Approval by the Telecom Secretary
 c. Approval by the Telecom Minister
 d. Expenditure Finance Committee

List-II
 i. Up to ₹100 crore
 ii. Finance Ministry
 iii. ₹500–1,000 crore
 iv. Up to ₹500 crore
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-i, c-iv and d-ii. Projects in the ₹500–1,000 crore range now go to the Expenditure Finance Committee, while the Telecom Secretary and Telecom Minister retain approval powers up to ₹100 crore and ₹500 crore respectively.

mcqs.question:
Match the Son river-related items with the correct description.

List-I
 a. Bansagar Agreement
 b. Source of the Son
 c. Course of the Son
 d. Confluence of the Son

List-II
 i. Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh
 ii. 1973 agreement involving Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and undivided Bihar
 iii. Joins the Ganga west of Patna
 iv. Flows through Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Bihar
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-i, c-iv and d-iii. The Bansagar Agreement was made in 1973 among Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and undivided Bihar; the Son rises at Amarkantak, crosses four States and joins the Ganga west of Patna.

mcqs.question: The decision concerning Tulu as an additional administrative language in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi was based on whose committee report?
mcqs.explanation: The decision was based on the committee of educationist M. Mohan Alva, whose report was submitted in 2023. The other names are associated with different political or administrative contexts in the listed developments.

mcqs.question: Which language is the official language of Karnataka?
mcqs.explanation: Kannada is the official language of Karnataka. Tulu is a Dravidian language connected with Tulu Nadu, but it is not the State's official language.
